title: Linearise a power-law model T = a l^b by taking logs, then read a and b off the gradient and intercept
content: When a model has the form y = a x^b (a power law), taking log10 of both sides gives log10 y = b log10 x + log10 a — a straight line when you plot log10 y against log10 x. The gradient of that line is the power b, and the y-intercept is log10 a, so a = 10^(intercept). If you're given two points on the log-log line, first find the gradient (b) from them using (change in log y)/(change in log x), then substitute one point (with your value of b) back into log10 y = b log10 x + log10 a to solve for log10 a, and hence a. Always write out the full equation y = a x^b at the end, not just the numerical values of a and b, if the question asks for 'a complete equation for the model'.
